# DC sub-task reparent via `PUT fields.parent` is accepted and IGNORED — the parent never moves

## Provenance

Surfaced live by harness run **30834117797** (job 91755000385, main @ `25ead49f3e`), by TWO
independent cells in opposite directions. Not predicted by any ticket; found only because story
5200's repaired cells read the field back instead of trusting the call's return.

## Evidence — two cells, and only one reading survives both

**Outbound (`test_outbound_set_subtask_parent_round_trips`)** — verbatim:

> the outbound parent set: fields.parent on RBJUUVX-3 is STILL 'RBJUUVX-1' — the parent it had
> BEFORE the mutation. Expected 'RBJUUVX-2'. This is the silent-no-op signature: `set_parent`
> writes `fields.parent` for a sub-task (`jira_datacenter/transport.py:711-712`) and every core
> caller swallows its failure (`dispatch_one.py:571-578` warns and continues), so an unchanged
> field is the ONLY place the failure is observable.

**Inbound (`test_inbound_set_subtask_parent_round_trips`)** — timed out after 90s / 45 attempts
waiting for `get_parent_map` to show the reparent; last parent seen was the ORIGINAL.

The inbound cell self-diagnoses as search-index lag ("NOT a bridge defect"). **That reading cannot
account for the outbound cell**, which read `fields.parent` back DIRECTLY over raw REST — no search
index involved — and still saw the pre-mutation value. A lagging index cannot make a direct field
read return stale data. The reading that explains BOTH is that the write itself never took effect.

## Why this matters more than one red cell

`transport.py:688-689` already carries a note that DC may **accept a `PUT {'parent': None}` and
ignore it**. This is the same accept-and-ignore shape on the SET path. If it holds, then the
sub-task branch of `set_parent` — the branch that exists precisely because it is supposed to be the
shape DC accepts — does not work on DC 8.17.1 at all.

That directly undercuts the premise of [rebar:39c1-2a32-b564-4b4b], whose mechanism analysis reads
"the one child shape DC accepts (sub-task)". If the sub-task write is also a no-op, then 39c1's
AC1 ("the emit gate and DC's accepted child shape overlap for at least one real configuration")
cannot be satisfied by the sub-task path, and the Epic Link path added in change 1302 becomes the
ONLY candidate rather than a second one.

## What is NOT yet established

Whether DC returns a success status for the ignored write, or an error that
`dispatch_one.py:571-578` swallows. The two have different fixes and the harness output does not
distinguish them — the swallow is exactly why. 39c1's AC4 alerting change (bridge_alerts entry on
every `set_parent` failure arm) will make the difference visible on the next run: an alert present
means DC errored and we hid it; no alert means DC returned success and lied.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] the live behaviour is established: does DC 8.17.1 return success, or an error, for a
      sub-task `PUT fields.parent` that does not take effect? Recorded with the run id and the
      raw response.
- [ ] if DC errors: the error is surfaced (39c1 AC4) and the caller stops reporting the mutation
      as applied
- [ ] if DC accepts-and-ignores: `set_parent` verifies the write by reading the field back, or the
      sub-task branch is declined the way the epic branch was, rather than silently claiming success
- [ ] a live cell proves the chosen path against the real instance — a unit suite CANNOT settle
      this (changes 1276 and 1288 were both mutation-proven and both wrong in production)
data.title: DC sub-task reparent via PUT fields.parent is accepted and ignored: the parent never moves
